newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Invesco investment head warns Argentina on jobless.
newsitem.headline: Invesco investment head warns Argentina on jobless.

text.p: Wendell Stark, the chief investment officer at Invesco Capital Management, said Tuesday there is concern among some investors that Argentina's high unemployment rate and political situation could derail reforms.
Investors fear that the pressures of high unemployment could lead to a change in policies "before the reforms really pay off", the head of the U.S. investment firm told a banking conference.
Argentina has come far with its reforms including the achievement of price stability for a sustained period, said Stark.
"But there is a feeling that there are still are problems," he added. Among them are a "nagging feeling" that efforts on the fiscal front could be softened in the face of elections.
In addition, "there is concern over a cumbersome tax system.
"There are real reasons why the upgrading process has taken time," he said, referring to the recent upgrade of Argentina's foreign currency debt rating by Standard & Poor's to BB from BB-.
On the other hand, Stark said his firm saw a very strong economy, boosted by export growth and productivity growth.
While he considers the external debt very high in relation to exports, he pointed to the success of Argentina's large international debt issues earlier this year as a positive signal.

He also voiced support of S&P's recent decision to lift the sovereign rating ceiling on several Argentine corporations and banks, which led to upgrades of up to two notches more than the sovereign rating. Some firms were upped to BBB-, an investment-grade rating.
There was "a rational basis of rating them (the firms) above the sovereign," he said.
He listed financial strength, earnings outside the country and securitization of debt issues as good reasons for the upgrades.

"It is not only important for the companies involved, but it raises the awareness of all Argentine companies," he said. The upgrades were a major event because they opened the way for more funds to invest in investment-grade rated firms.
"We see a very favorable environment for long-term investors," said Stark, whose company recently opened a regional office in Argentine. "The risk of Argentine investment is being steadily reduced."

One of the reasons for this is the efforts made by the government to extend its debt portfolio duration, something which lends confidence to the argument that "Argentine will in fact stay the course."
U.K. based Invesco is one of the largest global investment groups and has more than $90 billion of assets under management.
